ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper half (A) of the figure is a perspective photograph of a cuboid-style modern house; the lower half (B) gives the projection of the outline of this house in grid coordinates. In figure (B), it can be read that the endpoints of the left vertical edge are (0,0) and (0,3), the endpoints of the middle vertical edge are (22,-3) and (22,10), and the endpoints of the right vertical edge are (26,0) and (26,3). Reasoning: According to the vanishing point method, the roof edge of the long side passes through (0,3) and (22,10), and the ground edge passes through (0,0) and (22,-3). The equation of the roof edge is y = 3 + (7/22)x, and the equation of the ground edge is y = -(3/22)x. Set the two equal: 3 + (7/22)x = -(3/22)x, obtaining x = -6.6, and at this time y = 0.9. Therefore one horizontal vanishing point is on y = 0.9. The right side can also be verified: when the line passing through (22,10)-(26,3) and the line passing through (22,-3)-(26,0) intersect, likewise there is y = 0.9. So the horizon line is y = 0.9. In the perspective view, the horizon line corresponds to the image level of the camera height. On the left vertical edge, the ground is y = 0 and the roof is y = 3, corresponding to the real house height H = 3 m. The height ratio of the horizon line on this vertical edge is 0.9/3, therefore camera height = (0.9/3) × 3 m = 0.9 m.

raw_record.question_text: These days, there are so many stylish rectangular home-designs (see figure A). It is possible from the outline of those houses in their picture to estimate with good precision where the camera was. Consider an outline in one photograph of a rectangular house which has height H = 3 meters (see figure B for square-grid coordinates). Assume that the camera size is negligible, how high above the ground (in meters) was the camera at the moment this picture was taken?

method.method_draft: Use a vanishing-point construction. From figure B, read the projected house outline vertices: left vertical edge from (0,0) to (0,3), central vertical edge from (22,-3) to (22,10), and right vertical edge from (26,0) to (26,3). Identify the projected parallel roof/floor edges of the long side: the roof line through (0,3) and (22,10), and the floor line through (0,0) and (22,-3). Extend these two lines to their intersection; this gives one horizontal vanishing point with y-coordinate 0.9. Optionally verify with the right face: lines through (22,10)-(26,3) and (22,-3)-(26,0) meet at another vanishing point also on y=0.9. Therefore the horizon line is y=0.9. In perspective, the horizon is the image level of the camera height. On the left vertical edge, the ground is y=0 and the roof is y=3, corresponding to the real height H=3 m. The horizon cuts this vertical edge at 0.9/3 of the way up, so the camera height is (0.9/3)*3 = 0.9 m.

推理：按消失点方法，长侧面的屋顶边经过(0,3)与(22,10)，地面边经过(0,0)与(22,-3)。屋顶边方程为 y = 3 + (7/22)x，地面边方程为 y = -(3/22)x。令二者相等：3 + (7/22)x = -(3/22)x，得到 x = -6.6，此时 y = 0.9。因此一个水平消失点在 y = 0.9 上。右侧面也可验证：经过(22,10)-(26,3)的线与经过(22,-3)-(26,0)的线相交时同样有 y = 0.9。所以地平线为 y = 0.9。

透视图中，地平线对应相机高度的图像水平。左竖边上地面为 y = 0，屋顶为 y = 3，对应真实房屋高度 H = 3 m。地平线在该竖边高度比例为 0.9/3，因此相机高度 = (0.9/3) × 3 m = 0.9 m。

method.method_draft: Use a camera-height slice rather than explicitly finding vanishing points. From figure B, read the three projected vertical edges: left edge bottom/top y-values 0 and 3, central edge bottom/top y-values -3 and 10, and right edge bottom/top y-values 0 and 3. Let r be the fraction of the real 3 m height at which the camera lies, so the camera height is rH. Points of the building that are exactly at camera height project onto the horizon; because the visible verticals are vertical in the drawing, this horizon is horizontal, so these interpolated points must have the same y-coordinate on all vertical edges. For the left/right edges this y is 0 + 3r. For the central edge this y is -3 + 13r. Equate them: 3r = -3 + 13r, so r = 0.3. Then camera height = rH = 0.3 * 3 = 0.9 m.
